html:
A campaign by the communist Democratic Republic of Vietnam, from 1953 to 1956, to take land from landlords and give it to poor farmers. It turned violent, thousands were executed, and the party later admitted serious errors.

The campaign began in the last year of the First Indochina War, in areas held by the Viet Minh, and spread across the north after the French left in 1954. It followed the model of land reform in Mao's China, with Chinese advisers. Teams of cadres moved into villages, sorted every household into classes and held "struggle sessions" in which peasants denounced landlords before people's courts. Quotas pushed teams to find landlords even where there were few, and many were executed, including party members and families of soldiers. Estimates of the dead vary widely.

In 1956 Ho Chi Minh and the party admitted mistakes. The general secretary Trường Chinh lost his post, and General Võ Nguyên Giáp read a public self criticism. A "rectification of errors" freed prisoners and returned some land, but a peasant uprising in Nghệ An province that year was put down. Collective farming followed. See Vietnam.
sum: A campaign by the communist Democratic Republic of Vietnam, from 1953 to 1956, to take land from landlords and give it to poor farmers. It turned violent, thousands were executed, and the party later admitted serious errors.
